sides.name: Athens and Plataea
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Hoplites 10,000-11,000 incl. ~600-1,000 Plataeans (modern estimates, Wikipedia infobox). Light troops / armed slaves possibly present but unquantified, omitted. Weapons/armor between anchors 2 (1400 BCE) and 3 (300 BCE): bronze panoply, aspis, dory. Command 0.65: Miltiades, competent (rubric 0.5-0.75). Morale 0.9: existential defence of Athens. Training 0.4: citizen militia between levy (0.25) and conscript (0.5). riverCrossing false: the Athenians advanced across the open plain, no contested crossing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Marathon).

sides.name: Achaemenid expeditionary force (Datis, Artaphernes)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Modern consensus ~25,000 infantry (range 20,000-100,000 in the literature; low end set to 15,000 because part may have re-embarked). Ancient totals 100,000-600,000 (Nepos, Plutarch, Plato) rejected. Split ~1/3 spearmen, 2/3 archers is an educated guess from the sparabara spear-and-bow formation. ~1,000 cavalry unengaged per most modern readings, so mid 0. Lighter armor (linen/scale, wicker shields) than hoplites, armor 2.4. Comms/logistics 2.9: depot and relay-post system. Training 0.6: professional Persian/Saka core plus subject levies. prepared false: the Persians were drawn up on the open plain without works and were surprised by the Athenian advance at a run (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Marathon).

outcome.note: Athenian victory. Herodotus gives 192 Athenian dead (generally accepted: burial mound); wounded unknown, mid 500 is an educated guess. Persian dead 6,400 per Herodotus; other modern estimates 1,000-2,000; mid 5,000 placed between them (derived, grade C), 7 ships taken. Duration: "a long time" (Herodotus), a few hours. Date disputed (August or 12 September 490 BCE), dry season either way.
